Countersign — captioned walkthrough

Six scenes from a running local lab. Every frame is the app's own server-rendered markup with its own stylesheet — not a mockup, not a touched-up screenshot. Regenerate with node scripts/gen-walkthrough.mjs.

The model is not deterministic, and this page says so rather than picking a flattering run. Five runs of scene 5's exact sentence produced 3 signable mandates at $30.00 and 2 questions with no cap. The safety property held in all five — the cap was never raised toward the injected $1,000,000 — but the shape of the answer varies. Scene 5 shows a signable run because that is the only outcome displaying an amount at all; a question shows no number and would demonstrate nothing about the clamp.
Not a screen recording. The browser pane here was not compositing (visible: false), so a real screencast produced sixty seconds of one frozen frame and eight seconds of black; it was discarded rather than shipped. These are faithful static renders of the same pages, carrying the captions the recording would have carried.
Scene 01 / 06

Countersign — provable intent for agent payments on PayPal

A shopping agent needs to spend your money. Today it holds your card, so your only real choice is how much you trust it. Countersign gives it a signed spending limit instead.

Built for verifiable agent commerce on PayPal. Signed evidence helps explain authorization; it does not guarantee a dispute outcome or replace PayPal’s policies. Check regional and currency coverage.

Intent compiler

Say what you want. See what you would be signing.

A model reads your sentence and proposes spending limits. Everything below has then been checked against your own words by code that does not involve a model — and you can check that claim yourself, because the read-back is generated from the mandate rather than from the model’s reply.

Try: “Buy the cheapest trail runner under $80, and nothing else” · “Spend at most $50 on shoes at Northwind this month” · “Get me a waterproof jacket, up to 200 dollars, no subscriptions”

Payment sandbox. No live money moves in these demonstrations.

Intent compiler

Say what you want. See what you would be signing.

A model reads your sentence and proposes spending limits. Everything below has then been checked against your own words by code that does not involve a model — and you can check that claim yourself, because the read-back is generated from the mandate rather than from the model’s reply.

Try: “Buy the cheapest trail runner under $80, and nothing else” · “Spend at most $50 on shoes at Northwind this month” · “Get me a waterproof jacket, up to 200 dollars, no subscriptions”

This is what you would be authorising.

Every limit below came out of your own words. Nothing was invented by the model.

Read-back

What you are authorising

Spend at most $50.00 in total

Spend at most $50.00 per payment

Only at Northwind Outfitters

Pay only Northwind Outfitters

This mandate expires Sat 31 Oct, 10:39 PM IST

How we read your request

- We read notes "shoes" as a preference, not a limit. These are not signed and do not bound what the agent may buy.

Not covered

- Expiry: there is no automatic renewal. When this mandate expires the agent cannot spend under it again, even if it meant to.

The signed constraints (4) — machine-readable
[
  {
    "type": "mandate.checkout.allowed_merchants",
    "allowed": [
      {
        "id": "mrc_northwind",
        "name": "Northwind Outfitters",
        "website": "https://northwind.countersign.test"
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    "type": "mandate.payment.allowed_payees",
    "allowed": [
      {
        "id": "mrc_northwind",
        "name": "Northwind Outfitters",
        "website": "https://northwind.countersign.test"
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    "type": "mandate.payment.amount_range",
    "currency": "USD",
    "max": "5000 (minor units)"
  },
  {
    "type": "mandate.payment.budget",
    "currency": "USD",
    "max": "5000 (minor units)"
  }
]

Intent compiler · Countersign

Digits only, deliberately — a rounded guess inside a spending limit is the failure this product exists to prevent. No cap is emitted at all; the buyer is asked, and nothing is signable until they answer.

How we read your request

Where the model was overruled

The proposal contained something these rules did not accept. Each is recorded rather than silently applied.

Scene 05 / 06

Intent compiler · Countersign

The buyer wrote $30. The injected text says $1,000,000. The only amount in the mandate is $30.00 — the injected figure appears nowhere it would be signed. Across five runs of this exact sentence the cap was never exceeded; what varied was the outcome shape, and the note above records that.
